name: regina-rexx
why: A working interpreter for Rexx, an old scripting language from IBM mainframe lineage that most developers have never touched.

brief.what_it_is: Regina is an interpreter for Rexx, a programming language designed to be easy for beginners yet powerful enough for experienced users. It runs Rexx scripts on a wide range of operating systems, from Unix variants (Linux, FreeBSD, Solaris, AIX, HP-UX) to OS/2, Windows, Amiga, macOS, and PDAs. The homepage says Rexx is also well suited as a macro language embedded in other applications. The homepage does not describe the inputs and outputs in detail, so this is the general picture.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the project's two major goals are to be 100% compliant with the ANSI Standard and to be available on as many platforms as possible. The maintainer, Mark Hessling, says he has maintained it since 1993, with the support of the original author, Anders Christensen.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has a Download link but does not give installation steps, dependencies, or configuration. Brew lists five executables: regina, regina-config, rexx, rxqueue, and rxstack. The homepage does not explain what each one does.
brief.standout: Regina has been ported to an unusually wide set of platforms, including a Psion PDA (EPOC32) and a Zipit2 wireless messenger running an ARMv5 Debian port. The homepage also lists a large ecosystem of Rexx extensions, such as Rexx/SQL, Rexx/CURL, Rexx/Tk, Rexx/JSON, and RxSock.
brief.status: Maintained, with some evidence. The homepage shows current version 3.9.6 and says 'Last Updated: 14 January 2025'. The recent-changes list names 3.9.6 through 3.8.2 without dates, so I could not confirm the release date of 3.9.6 or the latest commit.
brief.caveats: The homepage notes that on Windows 9x and Me, all operating-system commands return a zero return code, because COMMAND.COM always does. The NT Resource Kit version is based on 0.07a and lacks later fixes. The ANSI compliance claim is the maintainer's own, made because no ANSI test suite was available to check it. The Regina Rexx Translation Project site is no longer available. The scout note's description of Rexx as having IBM mainframe lineage is not stated on the homepage. The homepage was fetched successfully, but it is a project web page, not a README, so no commands or install details were available.
quotes: Regina is a Rexx interpreter that has been ported to most Unix platforms

become 100% compliant with the ANSI Standard
Regina now implements all ANSI features, as far as I know.
